classification.description: A next generation HTTP client for Python. 🦋

plan.architecture_summary: HTTPX is a feature-rich HTTP client library for Python providing synchronous (httpx.Client) and asynchronous (httpx.AsyncClient) APIs. The top-level package exposes user-facing methods in _api.py, request/response models in _models.py, authentication flows in _auth.py, and exception classes in _exceptions.py. Transports in httpx/_transports/ decouple high-level client logic from low-level network execution, delegating core socket and HTTP protocol handling to httpcore. Additional modules handle content streams (_content.py), decoding (_decoders.py), and multipart form payloads (_multipart.py). Built-in support is also provided for ASGI and WSGI application testing via specialized transport classes.

key_directories.purpose: Core Python library codebase containing sync/async clients, models, authentication, and headers logic
Transport implementations (HTTPTransport, AsyncHTTPTransport, MockTransport, ASGITransport, WSGITransport)
Comprehensive pytest suite categorized by client, transport, and model components
Markdown documentation pages used to build the official project documentation website via MkDocs
Shell scripts automating installation, test running, linting, code checks, and local doc server preview

setup_steps.title: Clone the repository
setup_steps.detail: Clone your forked repository to your local computer.

setup_steps.title: Install dependencies
setup_steps.detail: Install HTTPX in editable mode along with all development and test dependencies.

setup_steps.title: Run the test suite
setup_steps.detail: Run the full pytest suite. Ensure ports 8000 and 8001 are free before executing.

setup_steps.title: Run linter and code checks
setup_steps.detail: Run code formatting and Mypy strict type checks.

setup_steps.title: Preview documentation
setup_steps.detail: Build and launch local documentation preview site using MkDocs.

branch: Create a topic branch on your personal fork and submit pull requests against the master branch.
commit: Keep commits atomic and focused on a single change.
Write clear and concise commit messages.
pull_request: Pull requests must include unit tests for code changes and update documentation as needed.
Fill out the pull request checklist in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md.
Substantial features or non-bugfix changes should ideally start as GitHub Discussions before PR submission.
code_style: Use 'scripts/lint' to auto-format code using Ruff.
Use 'scripts/check' to run linting and strict Mypy type-checking.
Use 'scripts/test' to run pytest suite (100% test coverage is enforced).

issues.title: Clean up imports in `__init.py__`
issues.why: It is a clean, beginner-friendly refactoring task that helps you understand the module layout of the codebase without risking runtime bugs.
issues.approach: Group exported items in httpx/__init__.py's __all__ list by their defining source module (such as _api.py, _auth.py, etc.) using comments as outlined in the issue description. Verify that all exported symbols remain present and run `scripts/check`.

issues.title: Document `Authentication` header is stripped on redirection
issues.why: It is a documentation issue requiring clear Python library usage explanation, making it an safe entry point.
issues.approach: Find the header handling documentation in docs/quickstart.md or docs/advanced/clients.md. Add a clear note explaining that Sensitive headers like Authorization are stripped across cross-origin redirects for security reasons.

issues.title: MockTransport doesn't set the elapsed property
issues.why: It involves writing clean Python code and tests for developer-facing mock utilities in httpx.
issues.approach: Update httpx/_transports/mock.py so MockTransport properly populates the elapsed response time or accepts a response time duration. Add tests in tests/test_transports.py to verify response.elapsed behavior when using MockTransport.

first_timer_insights: Recent merged PRs by first-time contributors often focus on small documentation fixes (e.g. fixing syntax errors in quickstart docs or adding third-party package references).
Code PRs from first-timers are generally small and contained (e.g. updating exports in httpx/__init__.py or updating test cases for external dependency compatibility).
All PRs must maintain 100% test coverage and pass Mypy strict type checks.
caveats: The test suite requires ports 8000 and 8001 to be free when running local integration tests.
Some optional features (HTTP/2, SOCKS, Brotli compression, CLI) require extra dependencies specified in pyproject.toml optional-dependencies.
